record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: In the prefix or suffix tree of a repetition-free language, does a given word generate a finite subtree or an infinite subtree?

evidence.quote: Does a given word generate a finite or infinite subtree?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $L \subseteq \Sigma^*$ be a repetition-free (i.e., power-free) language over a finite alphabet $\Sigma$, meaning that there is a fixed rational number $\alpha > 1$ (or an integer $k \ge 2$) such that no word in $L$ contains a factor of the form $u^\alpha$ (respectively $u^k$) with $u$ nonempty, and $L$ is closed under taking factors. The prefix tree $T_{\mathrm{pref}}(L)$ of $L$ is the rooted tree whose nodes are the words of $L$, with the empty word as the root, and in which the parent of a nonempty word $w \in L$ is obtained by deleting its last letter; the suffix tree $T_{\mathrm{suf}}(L)$ is defined analogously by deleting the first letter. For a word $w \in L$, the subtree rooted at $w$ in $T_{\mathrm{pref}}(L)$ consists of $w$ together with all of its descendants (i.e., all words in $L$ having $w$ as a prefix), and similarly for $T_{\mathrm{suf}}(L)$.

Problem. Given a repetition-free language $L$ and a word $w \in L$, decide whether the subtree of $T_{\mathrm{pref}}(L)$ (respectively $T_{\mathrm{suf}}(L)$) rooted at $w$ is finite or infinite. Equivalently, determine whether $w$ can be extended to the right (respectively to the left) by arbitrarily long words while remaining in $L$, or whether all such extensions have bounded length.
artifact.status_search_result: The decidability/structural question about whether a word generates a finite or infinite subtree in the prefix/suffix tree of a power-free language is part of an active line of research on prefix tree structure of repetition-free languages, where related questions (e.g., branching densities of square-free and cube-free words) remain open. No source found indicating a complete resolution.

status_evidence.title: Branching Densities of Cube-Free and Square-Free Words
status_evidence.snippet: Power-free languages contain numerous challenging open problems, with one group concerning the structure of prefix trees of infinite power-free languages.
status_evidence.claim: Structural questions about prefix trees of power-free languages remain open.
